requirements.requirement: Provide a WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080 containing the supplied project documents.
requirements.summary: Apache was active and listening on 8080; authenticated PROPFIND returned 207 and exposed brief.txt and budget.csv. Final comparisons showed both workspace files matched their supplied originals.

requirements.requirement: Allow the editor account from access.txt to create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: The configured editor account created a document with 201, read both expected versions, replaced it with 204, deleted it with 204, and subsequently received 404.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive locks so an update without the lock token cannot overwrite a locked document.
requirements.summary: Bounded tests before and after restart acquired exclusive locks, asserted a tokenless PUT returned 423, confirmed the original content remained unchanged, and successfully unlocked and deleted the test documents.

requirements.requirement: Deny anonymous access to the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous GET and PUT requests returned 401, including after restart and in the final observation.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: Final source digests matched the preparation baseline, and the preserved source files retained their original sizes, ownership, permissions, and content while matching the workspace copies.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 were unchanged after execution and restart. Apache 2.4.18 packages were installed from configured Xenial repositories.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed consistently with the fixed lifecycle observations, and service, authentication, documents, and locking were verified after recovery.
limitations: The fixed after-executor listening-sockets snapshot was empty even though direct commands observed the 8080 listener and successfully exercised the endpoint; this inconsistency slightly lowers confidence.

Some lock-result fields were redacted in captured stdout, so the expected 423 results are supported by the commands' successful explicit assertions and unchanged-content observations rather than visible numeric fields alone.
The first two post-restart lock probes failed because of script/test-state issues, but the final independent probe succeeded and cleaned its test document.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary managed-system mutation was identified: package installation, WebDAV configuration, service restart, CRUD/lock probes, cleanup, and the mandated node restart all had direct task or evidence roles. Two failed post-restart lock-verification attempts made bounded test-document mutations, but the document was deleted and a clean verification followed; no document residue remained (cmd-7ea6700cdd4242bf, cmd-2f4c2291cc494790, cmd-f7420acdde1145ba). Hygiene is reduced because six task-generated XML/header evidence files remained under /tmp. No failed services or package damage was observed.
